own_solution.law: Infinite-well eigenfunction psi_n = sqrt(2/L) sin(n pi x/L); P = [x/L - sin(2 n pi x/L)/(2 n pi)] evaluated from a to b
assumptions: ideal probe with unit efficiency inside the slice and zero outside
x measured from the left wall

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: T3E63 says the slice is widened by 0.24 nm without saying at which edge; widening at the right edge gives P = 0.3596, at the left edge 0.4594, symmetrically 0.4137, so the answer is not unique.
defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T3E63 omits both 'Before the position is measured' and 'at its right-hand edge' relative to T6A0A, so if they are meant as variants they differ in more than wording/attachment.

counterexamples: T3E63 with the 0.24 nm added at the left edge (slice 0.36-1.50 nm): P = 0.5 - (0.12 - sin(0.48 pi)/(4 pi)) = 0.4594, not 0.3596.
notes: Base: a/L = 0.2, b/L = 0.5. F(x) = x/L - sin(4 pi x/L)/(4 pi). F(b) = 0.5; F(a) = 0.2 - sin(0.8 pi)/(4 pi) = 0.2 - 0.58779/12.566 = 0.15323. P = 0.34677. Widened at right edge to 1.74 nm: F = 0.58 - sin(0.32 pi)/(4 pi) = 0.58 - 0.84433/12.566 = 0.51281; P = 0.35958. The problem introduces 'a second chip' without any first chip, which is slightly odd; 'coating is widened' is an odd phrase for thickening. Earlier-measurement and second-chip sentences are D.
